paragraphs: Avimi bar Nazi was his father-in-law. Adda bar Minyomi spoke to him. Rav Adda bar Mattana was Ravina the Earlier's pupil and Ravina the Later's colleague. Rav Aharon spoke to him. Ravina the Earlier with Rav Aha bar Rav (see there). Rav Aha was his son (see there, that he was a priest). Rav Aha of Difti spoke to him before Rava. Rav Aha bar Abaye spoke to him. Rav Aha bar Tahlifa spoke to him. Ravina the Later asked R' Aha bar Rava, ‘Can the master teach something about the partition?’ Rav Aha bar Bibi spoke to him in Rava's name. Amemar spoke to him. Rav Ashi (see above). Rav Ashi of Avira was in his time. Rav Gaza spoke to him. ‘Geniva said’—Ravina the Earlier. Rav Huna bar Rav Yehoshua ate one and Ravina ate eight. Rav Huna Mar bar Idi was in his time. Rav Huna bar Pappi was in his time. Rav Huna bar Mar Zutra spoke to him. Rav Huna bar Marimar before him. Mar Zutra bar Rav Tavi spoke to him. Mar Zutra bar Avdimi spoke to him. Mar Zutra bar Rav Huna bar Pappi spoke to him. Mar Zutra bar Rav Mari spoke to Ravina the Earlier. R' Ze'iri of Diyahavat spoke to him. Rav Haviva was his son—so Yuhasin writes; I have not found it. Also Rav Haviva. Rav Haviva of Sura on the Euphrates spoke to him. R' Hiyya bar Yitzhak permitted for him. Also R' Hama bar Buzi. R' Hanina of Sura on the Euphrates spoke to him. Rav Tavot spoke to him. Before Rav Yehudah of Difti. R' Yaakov bar Naftali was in his time—I have not found him mentioned. R' Yaakov of Nehar Pekod in his name. Rav Yitzhak bar Naftali spoke to him. R' Yirmeyah spoke to him. R' Yirmeyah of Difti was in his time. Mar was his son. Mar bar Rav Zutra before him. He called Mar bar Rav Ashi ‘master.’ Rav Mordekhai spoke to him. The matter involving Maryon bar Avin came before Ravina. The checked Bavli specifies people from his household. Marimar told him, ‘Thus your father said.’ Rav Mesharshiya bar Hanin spoke to him. Ravina said that Rav Mesharshiya son of Rav Natan told him a teaching. Rav Mesharshiya bar Rav Aha spoke to him. He spoke to Rav Mesharshiya. He asked Rav Nahman bar Yitzhak a question in Pesahim 105a. In a separate incident, he found him in Gittin 32b. Rav Natan. Rav Natan bar Ammi spoke to him. Also Rav Sama. Rav Sama bar Hilkiyah spoke to him. Rav Sama bar Ashi spoke to him. Rav Sama bar Rakta. Rav Sama bar Rav Mesharshiya. Rav Safra bar Yeiva spoke to him. He spoke to Rav Pappi. Rav bar Sheva before him. Rava bar Tahlifa spoke to him. He asked Rava, ‘What is the halakhah?’ Berakhot 33, beginning of b. He sat before Rava: there, 38a; and in Bava Batra 16b, Rava addressed him and Rav Hama bar Buzi as “children” (see above, R' Hama bar Buzi). He asked Rava, “May one drink urine on Shabbat?” (Shabbat 110a). He asked Rava, ‘What is your reasoning?’ Eruvin 47, end of b. When Ravina came to Mahoza, Rava’s place, his host brought him a knife to inspect. Ravina said, “Go, take it to Rava” (Eruvin 63a). He challenged Rava: Pesahim 12b. In Rava's name: there, 14a, 110, end of b; Bava Kamma 14a. Be’er Sheva (cited here as folio 92b) discusses Ravina speaking to Rava in Hullin 46b, Berakhot 15a and Sanhedrin 48b, and their successive statements in Ellu Metzi’ot (Bava Metzia 28a). Heilprin quotes Be’er Sheva’s first solution: “It appears this is not Ravina, Rav Ashi’s colleague,” since Rav Ashi was born on the day Rava died. The checked Be’er Sheva also explicitly cites Tosafot for the distinction. (It is puzzling that he writes ‘it appears’ as though the idea originated with him: see above, Ravina the Earlier, where Tosafot, Rosh, and Semag wrote this.) ‘Alternatively, the Rava here is not Rava bar Rav Yosef bar Hama, Abaye's colleague, but Rava bar Yitzhak’—see above, Rabbah bar Rav Yitzhak—‘Ravina's colleague, as is explicit in Eglah Arufah.’ (It appears he erred: Yuhasin writes that Rava bar Yitzhak was Rav's pupil, as also appears from his many ‘Rav said’ statements; see there. How could the Ravina in Eglah Arufah who accompanied Rava bar Yitzhak be Rav Ashi's colleague? Rather, that companion of Rava bar Yitzhak was Ravina the Earlier.) ‘Nevertheless, Sanhedrin 48b has Ravina speaking to Rava, Abaye's colleague, as is evident there.’ End quotation. Rabbah and Ravina: Ketubbot 102b; see Tosafot beginning ‘Rabbah and Ravina.’ Maginnei Shelomoh writes that Ran in Kiddushin identifies the Ravina paired here with Rabbah as the earlier Ravina. Maginnei Shelomoh also cites Milhamot on Kiddushin, where Ravina did not accept Rav Ashi’s ruling on the question under discussion. The checked Ran reads Rava in the parallel Kiddushin passage. Rabbah Zuti spoke to him. In Ravya bar Kisi's name. Rav Rehumi. Rafram. Rav Shmuel bar Zutra spoke to him. Rav Shemen of Sikhra spoke to him. Rav Shemaya was in his time. He spoke to Rav Sherevya. He asked Rav Sheshet: Bekhorot 15b; it appears this was Ravina the Earlier. Rav Tahlifa bar Gaza spoke to him.
